description: Exact RGBs in F2's final 16-color quantized palette eligible for palette-variant remapping. Only the top and trousers families are listed — skin (deep warm brown) and hair (black bun) are never remapped, matching the roster-integration structural decision (#2) and beingPalette.ts's existing remap-table shape (garment-only exact-RGB swap).

top.note: Dominant terracotta fill, verified clean via a strap-free torso patch (front rows 23-25) and cross-checked against the diagonal-strap band sample (no overlap).
Fold/sleeve highlight, only ~7 luminance steps above top-main; confirmed as a large clean block on the side view's chest/sleeve (rows 21-22), not a strap tone.

trousers.note: Dominant trousers fill below the waist row (hip_frac=0.73).
Leg-seam/fold shading, confirmed clean on both the front (row 37-38) and side (row 32-34) trouser columns.

excludedFromRemap.note: Verified by direct sampling (not ASCII legend alone): (119,58,25) reads as the diagonal crossbody-strap's main color in a dedicated strap-band sample AND independently as the side view's sleeve-shade tone — a multi-role color, excluded even though one of its roles borders the top. (18,18,18) is the touch-up's pupil tone but also occurs naturally in the bun's back-view shading, confirming it is a hair/eye tone, never a garment one. (84,46,24) is the bag-pouch shade tone (confirmed via a hip-bag patch sample), not a top color despite sitting one row above clean top territory in the front view.

suggestedVariant.name: moss
suggestedVariant.note: One example remap into the world's muted garment families (BEING_PALETTE_VARIANTS in beingPalette.ts: slate-blue / violet-grey / moss / ochre / bone) — F1 already used slate-blue, so this proposes moss for variety. Values keep the same luminance spacing as F2's own terracotta/trousers pair. Re-validate visually against the actual atlas render before locking in for R3.
